compare.building: Building… (the first RDKit call takes a few seconds)
compare.hint: Left: the main use case — a textbook-style condensed formula. Right: the same molecule's real 3D conformer. Drag it to rotate.
compare.title: 2D formula vs 3D conformer
compare.why.alanine: 2D can only hint at stereo with one hashed wedge. In 3D the stereocentre is visibly tetrahedral — that is where L/D comes from.
compare.why.aspirin: 2D cannot show the relative orientation of the ring, the ester and the acid; 3D does.
compare.why.benzene: The flat hexagon is correct, but 2D cannot show why: six π electrons are fully delocalised, so the ring is planar with equal C–C bond lengths.
compare.why.caffeine: 2D shows two fused rings; 3D shows they are coplanar and that the three methyls point in different directions.
compare.why.cyclohexane: 2D shows a regular hexagon. In 3D it is a chair: carbons alternate above and below, bond angles ~111° — a flat hexagon does not exist energetically.
compare.why.nicotine: 2D makes the two rings look merely adjacent; 3D shows their dihedral angle and the pyrrolidine ring's envelope conformation.
